stories.euphrates-tigris.title: Euphrates and Tigris
stories.euphrates-tigris.subtitle: From the mountains of Anatolia to the Shatt al-Arab
stories.euphrates-tigris.step.1: Two rivers rise within a hundred kilometres of each other in the highlands of eastern Anatolia. Their snowmelt has fed Mesopotamia for ten thousand years.
stories.euphrates-tigris.step.2: Since the 1970s a chain of dams on the Euphrates (Keban, Karakaya, Atatürk) holds back several years of the river's flow. The reservoirs are visible from space.
stories.euphrates-tigris.step.3: Downstream, the Euphrates runs at a fraction of its long-term mean in most years. Today's modelled flow is shown against the mean.
stories.euphrates-tigris.step.4: GRACE satellites measured one of the fastest groundwater declines on Earth in this basin between 2003 and 2009: about 144 km³ of stored water lost.
stories.euphrates-tigris.step.5: At the Shatt al-Arab the two rivers meet before the Gulf. Saltwater intrusion now reaches far upstream in dry summers.
stories.aral.title: The Aral Sea
stories.aral.subtitle: Two decades of shrinking, seen from orbit
stories.aral.step.1: In 1960 the Aral Sea was the fourth-largest lake on Earth. Irrigation of the Amu Darya and Syr Darya basins cut its inflow to a trickle.
stories.aral.step.2: GRACE has tracked the region's water storage since 2002. Slide back in time to watch the anomaly deepen.
stories.aral.step.3: The Kok-Aral dam (2005) stabilised the small northern sea; the eastern basin dried out completely in 2014.
stories.aral.step.4: Upstream reservoirs such as Toktogul now hold the water that once reached the sea.
stories.colorado.title: The Colorado
stories.colorado.subtitle: Lake Mead, Lake Powell and a river that rarely reaches the sea
stories.colorado.step.1: The Colorado supplies forty million people. Its flow is allocated by a 1922 compact based on unusually wet years.
stories.colorado.step.2: Lake Mead's surface area, tracked by satellite, shows the drawdown of the 2000s megadrought and the partial recovery after wet winters.
stories.colorado.step.3: Lake Powell, upstream, buffers the Upper Basin states. Its fill proxy is shown against the last three years.
stories.colorado.step.4: The drought layer shows the Copernicus Combined Drought Indicator across the basin, refreshed every ten days.
stories.colorado.step.5: In the delta the river usually ends in the sand before reaching the Gulf of California.
stories.alps.title: Alpine glaciers
stories.alps.subtitle: The fastest-retreating ice in the inventory
stories.alps.step.1: Central Europe has lost roughly a third of its glacier volume since 2000. WGMS reports the regional balance every year.
stories.alps.step.2: The Aletsch, the largest glacier in the Alps, has retreated more than three kilometres since 1870.
stories.alps.step.3: Where the regional mass balance is negative, glacier edges pulse gently in this map — a reminder that the ice is thinning.
stories.alps.step.4: Glacier melt still sustains the Rhône, Rhine and Po in late summer. As the ice shrinks, that summer buffer shrinks with it.
